method: Decoding is framed as a tree search over an absorbing-state discrete diffusion model with probability beam search, supplemented by an LP-relaxation dual bound and a distance-based test derived from the code to certify per-frame global ML optimality.
result: Across several codes and operating points, the decoder certifies a large fraction of frames, the two tests divide frames as predicted, certification serves as a reliability signal, and the decoder is competitive with neural baselines and near exact ML references.
conclusion: Certified decoding can provide per-frame optimality guarantees without accuracy-computation trade-offs on certified frames, but the work concerns classical error-correcting codes and is not directly connected to quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Cryptanalysis On Two Feistel-Type Constructions
authors: Yan-Ying Zhu, Bin-Bin Cai, Fei Gao, Song Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, the security of traditional cryptographic systems is facing significant challenges. As a fundamental component of symmetric cryptography, block ciphers have attracted increasing attention regarding their quantum security in recent years. In this paper, we propose new quantum attacks on two Feistel-type constructions, i.e., New Structure IV and the lightweight block cipher LBlock, under the quantum chosen-plaintext attack (qCPA) model. First, we construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and perform an [MATH]-round quantum key-recovery attack. Compared with Li et al.'s qCPA-based result presented at INSCRYPT 2024, our attack reduces the time complexity by a factor of [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the subkey length. Second, we design a 9-round quantum distinguisher for LBlock and extend it to an [MATH]-round quantum key-recovery attack. The proposed quantum distinguisher covers one more round than Liu et al.'s automated-search distinguisher at ASIACRYPT 2025, which results in a [MATH] reduction in the time complexity of our [MATH]-round quantum key-recovery attack on LBlock. Furthermore, by analyzing the structure of the round function and the key scheduling of LBlock, we reduce the subkey guess space for the 15-round attack from 76 bits to 52 bits, lowering the time complexity from \(O(2^{38})\) to \(O(2^{26})\) by a factor of \(2^{12}\).
tldr: The paper develops new quantum chosen-plaintext attacks on two Feistel-type block ciphers, New Structure IV and LBlock, improving distinguisher rounds and key-recovery time complexity over prior results.
motivation: Growing quantum computing power threatens classical symmetric cryptography, so understanding the quantum security of block ciphers has become important; existing qCPA distinguishers and key-recovery attacks on Feistel constructions leave room for improvement.
method: The authors construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and a 9-round distinguisher for LBlock within the qCPA model, then extend these to full-round quantum key-recovery attacks, exploiting the round function and key schedule of LBlock to prune the subkey guess space.
result: The New Structure IV attack reduces time complexity by a factor of 2^(k/2) relative to Li et al. (INSCRYPT 2024); the LBlock distinguisher covers one extra round compared with Liu et al. (ASIACRYPT 2025), and the 15-round attack's subkey guess space shrinks from 76 to 52 bits, lowering complexity from O(2^38) to O(2^26).
conclusion: Quantum cryptanalysis meaningfully weakens these Feistel-type ciphers, underscoring the need for quantum-resistant symmetric designs and deeper study of qCPA-based attack models.

title: Information, Estimation, And Prediction For Discrete Memoryless Channels Via Poissonization
authors: Tsachy Weissman Abhiram Gorle
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop information--estimation relations for an arbitrary discrete memoryless channel with finite input and output alphabets by varying the expected number of observations while keeping the channel fixed. A single hidden input is observed through a Poisson number of conditionally independent channel uses, whose mean specifies the observation budget. The derivative of mutual information with respect to this budget equals the minimum expected relative-entropy loss for estimating the input's output distribution. The posterior average of the channel's output distributions achieves this minimum and is the Bayesian predictor for the next observation. When the input distribution, the channel, or both are misspecified, the relative entropy between the true and assumed observation laws is the integral of the excess prediction loss over the budget. We also extend these relations to finite-state processes taking values in the input alphabet and observed through the channel at independent Poisson sampling times. Both in the matched setting and under model mismatch, the expected prediction loss accumulated over time using past observations equals the corresponding loss using the full observation record (noncausal estimation), averaged over lower sampling rates.
tldr: The paper derives information-estimation-prediction relations for classical discrete memoryless channels by Poissonizing the number of channel observations.
motivation: It aims to connect derivatives of mutual information with minimum expected estimation and prediction losses under varying observation budgets, including model mismatch.
method: A hidden input is observed through a Poisson number of conditionally independent channel uses; the analysis relates mutual-information derivatives to Bayesian prediction loss and relative entropy.
result: The derivative of mutual information equals the minimum expected relative-entropy loss, achieved by the posterior average output distribution; under misspecification, relative entropy is the integral of excess prediction loss over budget.
conclusion: The work provides classical information-theoretic estimation and prediction identities for discrete memoryless channels and finite-state processes, with no direct quantum information extension.

title: Short Point Lists For CNFs And Stronger Constant-Depth Circuit Hardness
authors: Yan Zhong Xin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a short-description decomposition of bounded-width CNFs. For every fixed [MATH], every width-[MATH] CNF on [MATH] variables is an exact disjoint union of at most [MATH] width-[MATH] CNFs, each determined by [MATH] satisfying assignments. For every fixed [MATH], we prove a worst-case size lower bound of [MATH] against depth-at-most-[MATH] unbounded-fan-in AND/OR circuits with input negations for three polynomial-time Boolean families: inverse trace over binary fields, the Goldreich--Tal trilinear function, and OpenAI's polynomial evaluator with its original parameters. All parameter bits count as inputs. For inverse trace, every such circuit of size at most [MATH], where [MATH], has uniform sign correlation at most [MATH]. Here [MATH] depend only on [MATH]. This improves on the classical parity correlation bound. The lower bounds combine the decomposition with restriction arguments; the correlation bound additionally uses common partial decision trees. We also construct exact nonuniform AND/OR circuits for inverse trace of size [MATH] at depth eight and [MATH] at depth nine. For every fixed integer [MATH], the construction gives depth-[MATH] circuits of size [MATH]. The upper bounds implement finite-field evaluation and interpolation using circuits that enumerate intermediate states.
tldr: The paper gives a short-description decomposition of bounded-width CNFs and uses it, together with restriction arguments, to prove worst-case size lower bounds against constant-depth unbounded-fan-in AND/OR circuits for three polynomial-time Boolean families, including inverse trace over binary fields.
motivation: The authors aim to strengthen constant-depth circuit hardness results beyond the classical parity correlation bound, targeting explicitly given polynomial-time Boolean functions such as inverse trace, the Goldreich--Tril trilinear function, and OpenAI's polynomial evaluator.
method: They decompose every width-w CNF on n variables into a disjoint union of small width-w CNFs each fixed by few satisfying assignments, then combine this decomposition with restriction arguments; the sign-correlation bound additionally employs common partial decision trees.
result: They obtain a worst-case size lower bound of exp(Omega(n^{1/(d-1)})) against depth-d AND/OR circuits with negations for the three families, and a uniform sign correlation bound for inverse trace that improves on the parity correlation bound; they also construct exact nonuniform circuits of size exp(O(n^{1/(d-1)})) at each fixed depth.
conclusion: The work establishes near-tight constant-depth circuit lower and upper bounds for concrete polynomial-time functions, advancing classical circuit complexity rather than quantum information theory.

title: Quantum-Seeded Distributed Post-Quantum Group Signatures For 5g V2x Communications
authors: P. Blanco-Casal, P. Rejo-Iglesias, D. Cajaraville-Aboy, J. Vecino-Pe\~nas, R. P. D\'iaz-Redondo, A. Fern\'andez-Vilas, M. Fern\'andez Veiga
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications rely on elliptic-curve signatures that a quantum adversary breaks and on pseudonym certificates whose anonymity rests on rotation rate, not cryptography. This work presents qDGSP, a post-quantum V2X infrastructure: a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP, over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+) distributed between a central controller and roadside verifiers. Group keys derive deterministically from quantum key distribution (QKD) seeds served over the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, so no group-signature secret crosses the classical channel. qDGSP-EA (Ephemeral Association) binds an ephemeral ML-DSA-65 key to one group signature per 5G cell: messages remain unlinkable across cells, linkable within one. On a testbed with emulated 5G links, median end-to-end latency stayed within the 100ms ETSI budget for every variant. The qDGSP-EA intra-cell DENM matched the NIST ML-DSA-65 baseline on the wire, and under load EA mode raised delivery from roughly 78% to 93%.
tldr: qDGSP is a post-quantum V2X group-signature infrastructure that derives hash-based group keys from QKD seeds delivered over the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, with an ephemeral-association variant for cell-level unlinkability.
motivation: V2X communications currently rely on elliptic-curve signatures that are broken by quantum adversaries and pseudonym certificates whose anonymity depends only on rotation rate rather than cryptography.
method: The authors build a distributed dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP) over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+ split between a central controller and roadside verifiers, seeding group keys deterministically from QKD-derived secrets, and add an Ephemeral Association mode binding per-cell ML-DSA-65 keys to one group signature.
result: On an emulated 5G testbed, median end-to-end latency stayed within the 100 ms ETSI budget for all variants; EA mode matched the NIST ML-DSA-65 baseline on the wire for intra-cell DENM and raised message delivery from roughly 78% to 93% under load.
conclusion: QKD-seeded post-quantum group signatures are feasible for latency-constrained V2X deployment and can improve delivery under load while providing cryptographic rather than rotation-based anonymity.

title: Energy Consumption Of Post-Quantum Cryptography On Constrained And General-Purpose Architectures
authors: Olivier Gillot, William J. Buchanan, Madjid G. Tehrani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With Q-day approaching, the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) has begun, with governments across the US, UK and EU mandating migration to quantum-resistant standards. This paper benchmarks the three NIST-standardised PQC algorithms - FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) - across key generation, signing and verification operations, measuring both computational performance and energy consumption on a range of constrained IoT-class devices, from the 32-bit Raspberry Pi 1 and Zero to the 64-bit Raspberry Pi 4, as well as commodity laptop hardware. Using the FNIRSI FNB58 USB power meter and OpenSSL~3.5, results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA achieve energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography across all tested architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing is inadvisable on constrained hardware: energy costs for SLH-DSA signing on 32-bit devices were up to 243\% higher than on equivalent 64-bit hardware, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments. These findings have direct implications for IoT security practitioners planning PQC migration.
tldr: The paper benchmarks energy consumption and runtime of the three NIST-standardised post-quantum cryptography algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) across IoT-class and commodity hardware.
motivation: With governments mandating migration to quantum-resistant standards ahead of Q-day, practitioners need practical data on whether PQC is viable on resource-constrained IoT devices.
method: Using OpenSSL 3.5 and an FNIRSI FNB58 USB power meter, the authors measure key generation, signing and verification costs for ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA on Raspberry Pi 1/Zero/Pi 4 and laptops, comparing against classical elliptic-curve cryptography.
result: ML-KEM and ML-DSA show energy and speed efficiency comparable to ECC across all tested architectures, whereas SLH-DSA signing on 32-bit devices costs up to 243% more energy than on 64-bit hardware.
conclusion: ML-KEM and ML-DSA are practical for IoT deployment, but SLH-DSA signing is inadvisable on constrained 32-bit hardware, informing PQC migration planning for IoT security practitioners.

title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference With Plasmonic Metasurfaces
authors: Lawrence M. Qin, Sky Semone, Matthew J. Brandsema, Christos Argyropoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.
tldr: The paper designs a plasmonic metasurface that acts as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter to control single-photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference.
motivation: Efficiently controlling optical quantum interference on a single device could enable key operations for quantum information processing, such as quantum optical logic gates.
method: A composite quantum plasmonic metasurface is proposed, combining a periodically nanoslit-corrugated plasmonic grating for extraordinary optical transmission with top nanostripes forming nanocavities with localized gap plasmon resonances; performance is analyzed via a quantum coalescence metric.
result: The device can switch between photon bunching and anti-bunching by varying incident photon frequency or design dimensions, demonstrating controllable quantum interference.
conclusion: The metasurface provides a compact platform for non-classical light interaction control and may be useful for applied quantum optical logic gates in computing and communications.

title: Boundary One-Point Functions In The Open Xxz Spin Chain With Generic Integrable Boundaries
authors: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.
tldr: The paper computes exact boundary one-point functions in the open XXZ spin chain with generic integrable boundary conditions using functional separation of variables.
motivation: Correlation functions and form factors in open integrable spin chains with generic boundaries are difficult because the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the Baxter TQ equation becomes inhomogeneous.
method: The authors adapt the functional separation of variables method, previously developed for rational quasi-periodic chains, to open XXZ chains with diagonal and generic integrable boundaries, deriving determinant expressions for boundary-spin one-point functions.
result: Exact finite-size determinant formulae are obtained for longitudinal and transverse boundary one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates, verified against direct finite-volume diagonalization.
conclusion: Functional separation of variables remains effective for generic integrable boundaries and provides a route to exact observables beyond the spectrum in open XXZ chains.

title: Testing Tls 1.3 Pqc On Constrained Devices And Microcontrollers
authors: Olivier Gillot, William J. Buchanan, Callum Turino
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The UK, EU and US governments have set timelines for post-quantum cryptography migration of critical systems, with deadlines ranging from 2028 to 2035. This paper focuses on IoT-class devices and microcontrollers and the viability of using PQC to connect these devices in secure TLS 1.3 connections. Using wolfSSL, we benchmark a 36-combination TLS 1.3 algorithm matrix, pairing ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and X25519/ECC P-256 key exchange with ML-DSA-44/65/87, Ed25519, ECDSA, and RSA-PSS authentication, across four devices (Raspberry Pi Pico W & Pico 2 W, ESP32, and a Raspberry Pi Zero), measuring both handshake latency and energy consumption. We found that in capable devices, all choices in the TLS matrix gave similar results, but that in IoT-class devices, PQC performance is highly implementation- and architecture-dependent: the common assumption that elliptic-curve key exchange must be cheaper than post-quantum lattice-based key exchange does not hold in this wolfSSL-based implementation, where the best full-PQC combination (ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44) completes TLS handshakes 41% faster than the equivalent classical-modern pairing (X25519 + RSA-PSS) on the Pico W (up to 2.12x as energy-efficient, depending on the paired authentication algorithm), and 8.9x faster on the ESP32. Full-PQC, ML-KEM-512/ML-DSA-44, is not only possible but energy-competitive with or superior to Hybrid or Elliptic Curve alternatives on the most constrained devices, though ML-DSA's variable signing time means applications with strict latency-predictability budgets must accept this variance as the cost of full quantum-safe authentication. We further show that the IETF's draft-specified X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid incurs approximately the combined cost of its two components, rather than offering a performance compromise, making pure ML-KEM the more practical choice on hardware lacking Curve25519 assembly support.
tldr: Benchmarks a 36-combination TLS 1.3 post-quantum/classical algorithm matrix (ML-KEM, X25519, ECC, ML-DSA, Ed25519, ECDSA, RSA-PSS) on IoT-class devices and microcontrollers, measuring handshake latency and energy.
motivation: Governments have set 2028-2035 migration deadlines for post-quantum cryptography, but the feasibility and cost of PQC handshakes on highly constrained IoT hardware is unclear, and common assumptions about the relative expense of elliptic-curve versus lattice-based key exchange may not hold.
method: Using wolfSSL on a Raspberry Pi Pico W, Pico 2 W, ESP32, and Raspberry Pi Zero, the authors benchmark handshake latency and energy consumption across a 36-combination TLS 1.3 algorithm matrix pairing ML-KEM-512/768/1024 and X25519/ECC P-256 key exchange with ML-DSA-44/65/87, Ed25519, ECDSA, and RSA-PSS authentication.
result: On capable devices all combinations perform similarly, but on constrained devices performance is strongly implementation- and architecture-dependent: full-PQC ML-KEM-512 + ML-DSA-44 completes handshakes 41% faster than X25519 + RSA-PSS on the Pico W (up to 2.12x more energy-efficient) and 8.9x faster on the ESP32; the X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid costs roughly the sum of its parts rather than providing a compromise.
conclusion: Full post-quantum TLS is practical and energy-competitive on the most constrained microcontrollers, though ML-DSA's variable signing time imposes latency-predictability costs, and pure ML-KEM is preferable to hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 on hardware lacking Curve25519 assembly support.

title: Two Routes To The Hadamard Condition
authors: Eleanor March
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum field theory on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable', 'vacuum-like' states of linear quantum fields, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. In this paper, I strengthen, generalise, and bring under technical control two popular motivations for the Hadamard condition - one which appeals to the role of Hadamard states in defining physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator on general curved spacetime backgrounds, and one which appeals to the equivalence principle. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
tldr: A foundations-of-physics analysis that strengthens and generalizes two motivations for the Hadamard condition on states of linear quantum fields in curved spacetime.
motivation: The Hadamard condition is usually justified informally as characterizing 'physically reasonable' or 'vacuum-like' states; the author aims to place its two standard motivations—well-definedness of Wick polynomials and the stress-energy expectation value, and the equivalence principle—on firmer technical footing.
method: Conceptual and mathematical analysis within algebraic/axiomatic quantum field theory on curved spacetimes, examining the microlocal spectrum condition and its consequences for renormalized observables.
result: Generalized and technically controlled versions of both routes to the Hadamard condition are given, clarifying its relation to the equivalence principle and the precise sense in which Hadamard states are vacuum-like.
conclusion: The paper clarifies the status of the Hadamard condition as a foundational constraint in curved-spacetime QFT, though it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid platforms.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

title: Quantum Algorithm For High-dimensional Nonlinear Stochastic Differential Equations Based On Carleman Linearization
authors: Koichi Miyamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Addressing nonlinear numerical problems in quantum computing remains challenging, but several approaches, including Carleman linearization (CL), have been proposed to construct quantum algorithms for such problems. In this work, we develop a CL-based method for a high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equation (SDE) [MATH] for an [MATH]-valued random process [MATH], aiming at quantum speed-up with respect to the dimension [MATH]. We introduce auxiliary processes [MATH] that approximate [MATH], derive a linearized system of SDEs for them, and obtain the linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) governing their expectations. We then apply a quantum ODE solver to it and, from the resulting quantum state, extract an estimate for the expectation of a linear function of [MATH] by overlap estimation. We show that, provided the nonlinear and noise terms in the SDE are sufficiently small relative to the linear term, the CL error decreases exponentially with the truncation order [MATH] in CL, and we can estimate the target expectation with a [MATH] number of queries to unitaries encoding coefficient matrices [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. Finally, we also run a numerical demonstration for an SDE related to Langevin dynamics, observing the exponential decay of the CL error as [MATH] increases.
tldr: The paper develops a Carleman-linearization-based quantum algorithm for high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equations, targeting quantum speed-up in dimension.
motivation: Nonlinear numerical problems, especially high-dimensional stochastic differential equations, remain difficult for quantum algorithms despite proposals such as Carleman linearization.
method: Auxiliary processes are introduced to approximate the target process, a linearized SDE system is derived for their expectations, and a quantum ODE solver plus overlap estimation extracts the desired expectation.
result: Under small nonlinear and noise terms relative to the linear term, the Carleman truncation error decays exponentially with truncation order, and the target expectation is estimated with polylogarithmic query complexity; a numerical Langevin-type demonstration supports the error decay.
conclusion: The work extends Carleman-linearization quantum algorithms to high-dimensional nonlinear SDEs, but it sits outside the researcher's focused quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Reverse Module Categories Of Vertex Operator Algebras
authors: Chongying Dong, Binghui Li, Li Ren, Yilong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.
tldr: The paper proves that the reverse braided module category of a rational vertex operator algebra admits a realization that is preserved under cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds, and verifies this for Virasoro minimal models, affine VOAs of type ABCDE, and related W-algebras and parafermion VOAs.
motivation: The reverse braided category of the module category of a rational VOA is a structural object whose realizability (e.g. as modules of another VOA or as a category of local modules) underpins constructions in rational conformal field theory and its orbifold/coset relations; a systematic proof of preservation under standard algebraic constructions was missing.
method: The authors use holomorphic extensions of VOAs and commutant (coset) constructions within the framework of braided tensor categories of modules, establishing closure of the realization property under cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds.
result: The realization property is shown to be stable under these constructions, and is then established explicitly for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine VOAs of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, principal W-algebras of type ADE, and associated parafermion VOAs.
conclusion: The results give a broad structural toolkit for identifying reverse braided module categories in rational CFT, covering many of the standard rational model families used in mathematics and mathematical physics.

title: Linear Preservers Of Semipositivity Over Proper Cones
authors: Jinli Xu Yulong Tian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all real linear operators on [MATH], with [MATH], that preserve semipositivity between two prescribed pairs of proper cones, without assuming invertibility. Every such operator has product form [MATH] or degenerate form [MATH], possibly both. We give necessary and sufficient cone conditions for each form; the degenerate condition is expressed through a linear matrix pencil on the dual of the target output cone. The degenerate preservers are exactly those of operator rank [MATH], and every preserver of larger rank has product form. We also classify all linear preservers from [MATH] to [MATH] over the nonnegative orthants, obtaining three disjoint classes, including two rank-three classes outside product form.
tldr: The paper classifies real linear operators that preserve semipositivity between prescribed pairs of proper cones, including degenerate and product-form preservers.
motivation: Linear preserver problems are fundamental in matrix analysis and operator theory, and semipositivity over proper cones generalizes positivity under cone orderings.
method: The authors give a complete classification of semipositivity-preserving linear maps without assuming invertibility, deriving necessary and sufficient cone conditions and using a linear matrix pencil characterization for degenerate preservers.
result: Every preserver has product form or degenerate form, with degenerate preservers exactly those of a specified operator rank; for nonnegative orthants, three disjoint classes are obtained, including two rank-three classes outside product form.
conclusion: The work provides a general structural classification of cone semipositivity preservers, extending linear preserver theory beyond the invertible or standard positive-semidefinite settings.

title: Symmetry And Quantum Interference In The Attosecond Domain
authors: C. Figueira de Morisson Faria, S. Hashim, J. Rivera-Dean, T. Rook
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.
tldr: This review examines symmetry and quantum interference in attosecond strong-field photoelectron dynamics, including holography and nonsequential double ionization.
motivation: The authors aim to synthesize how tailored laser fields and quantum-orbit methods can control and interpret dynamical symmetries and interference pathways in ultrafast electron dynamics.
method: The review draws on the authors' own work to connect photoelectron momentum distributions to ionization, propagation, and rescattering pathways using quantum-orbit methods.
result: It identifies several forms of quantum interference in ultrafast photoelectron holography and recollision-excitation double ionization, and discusses how target properties and nonclassical light modify these processes.
conclusion: The paper highlights opportunities for controlling strong-field electron dynamics via symmetry and quantum interference, especially using nonclassical states of light.

title: Time-resolved Rydberg Dynamics In Molecules
authors: Erfan Saydanzad, Van-Hung Hoang, Uwe Thumm
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general theoretical framework for the ultrafast dynamics of coherently populated autoionizing Rydberg states in molecules, whose coherent decay results in asymmetric Fano line shapes produced by interference between resonant autoionization and direct ionization. The asymmetric line shapes form in the photoelectron continuum during the autoionization lifetime of the decreasing Rydberg population. By parameterizing autoionization resonances and solving the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation, we model the buildup of the Fano profile together with the decline of the coherently excited Rydberg-state population. We compare our calculated photoelectron yields with the XUV-pump--IR-probe photoemission experiment of Biswas et al., Phys. Rev. A 110, 043106 (2024), in which neutral ground-state CO[MATH] molecules are excited by an XUV pulse to the Henning sharp and diffuse Rydberg series and subsequently ionized by the delayed IR pulse. Based on our numerically modeled photoelectron yields, we analyze two complementary processes: (i) photoemission into the [MATH] continuum of residual CO[MATH] ions, which exposes interferences between direct photoionization and excited-state autoionization, and (ii) IR-induced photoemission into the CO[MATH][[MATH]] continuum, which reveals quantum beats between Rydberg states. Our close-coupling model provides a versatile, extendable framework for tracking molecular Rydberg-state relaxation and, more generally, light-driven coherent dynamics in complex quantum systems.
tldr: The paper develops a time-dependent theoretical model for ultrafast autoionizing Rydberg-state dynamics in molecules and compares it with XUV-pump–IR-probe photoemission experiments on CO.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how asymmetric Fano line shapes build up during the finite lifetime of coherently excited molecular Rydberg states and how quantum beats between Rydberg states appear in time-resolved photoemission.
method: They parameterize autoionization resonances and solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation in a close-coupling framework, modeling photoelectron yields for XUV excitation followed by delayed IR ionization.
result: The calculated photoelectron yields reproduce and interpret experimental spectra, exposing interference between direct photoionization and autoionization as well as IR-induced quantum beats in the CO+ continuum.
conclusion: The framework provides an extendable approach for tracking molecular Rydberg-state relaxation and light-driven coherent dynamics in complex quantum systems.

title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Methods For Optimization: Lessons From Classical Decomposition
authors: David E. Bernal Neira
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum and physics-inspired solvers provide specialized sampling interfaces for Ising and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization models, but constrained optimization requires broader coordination and certification. This survey uses classical decomposition to analyze how such solvers can be integrated into hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. We distinguish formal decomposition, reformulation and reduction, and computational orchestration. For each interface, we ask what the transformation preserves, which assumptions make the outer method converge, and which certificates the implemented inner routine supplies. The central questions are whether that information meets the classical algorithm's requirements and whether hybridization improves solution quality or total cost enough to justify its coordination overhead. Benders decomposition, column generation, graph reduction, and copositive methods illustrate this distinction by separating heuristic proposals from classical certification. We also distinguish component effects within a fixed wrapper, reduction--solver interactions, and comparisons between complete quantum-enabled and classical systems. The analyzed studies provide conditional component benefits and favorable co-design evidence, but do not establish transferable end-to-end superiority over strong classical comparators. The resulting framework identifies opportunities for constraint programming and operations research in structure-preserving design, safeguarded hybrid algorithms, and controlled benchmarking.
tldr: This survey analyzes hybrid quantum-classical optimization through the lens of classical decomposition, asking what information quantum or physics-inspired solvers must supply to support classical certification and convergence.
motivation: Quantum and physics-inspired solvers offer specialized sampling for Ising and QUBO models, but constrained optimization requires broader coordination and certification than these solvers alone provide.
method: The paper distinguishes formal decomposition, reformulation/reduction, and computational orchestration, and examines interfaces such as Benders decomposition, column generation, graph reduction, and copositive methods.
result: The analyzed studies show conditional component benefits and favorable co-design evidence, but do not establish transferable end-to-end superiority over strong classical comparators.
conclusion: The framework identifies opportunities for constraint programming and operations research in structure-preserving design, safeguarded hybrid algorithms, and controlled benchmarking.

title: Cramer-Rao Type Bounds For Generalized Exponential Families
authors: M Ashok Kumar Satyajit Dhadumia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that the sufficient statistics of an exponential family attain the usual Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) for their expected value. In this paper, we extend this result to a broader family of distributions that includes exponential families and power-law families, with Student t-distributions as special case. To derive the generalized Cramer-Rao inequality, we first apply Eguchi's theory to Bregman divergence to obtain a Riemannian metric and then follow the approach of Amari and Nagaoka. Since this approach applies only to models with finite support, we use Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to extend it to models with countably infinite or continuous support. The resulting generalized CRLB provides a finite-sample lower bound related to the asymptotic covariance matrix of the Minimum Bregman Divergence Estimator (MBDE). We show that the sufficient statistic of the generalized family attains the generalized CRLB. Moreover, although the generalized CRLB does not, in general, coincide with the asymptotic covariance matrix of the MBDE, the covariance matrix of an estimator attaining the generalized CRLB coincides with the corresponding matrix for the joint distribution of the sample.
tldr: This paper derives generalized Cramer-Rao lower bounds for a broad class of distributions including exponential and power-law families using information geometry and Bregman divergence.
motivation: The usual Cramer-Rao lower bound is known for exponential families, and the authors aim to extend it to more general families such as power-law and Student-t distributions.
method: The authors use Eguchi's theory of Bregman divergence to obtain a Riemannian metric, follow the Amari-Nagaoka approach for finite-support models, and extend to countable or continuous support via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
result: They obtain a finite-sample generalized Cramer-Rao bound related to the asymptotic covariance of the Minimum Bregman Divergence Estimator and show that sufficient statistics of the generalized family attain the bound.
conclusion: The generalized bound does not generally equal the MBDE asymptotic covariance, but the covariance matrix of an estimator attaining it coincides with that of the joint sample distribution.

title: Efficient Perturbation-Based Sc Decoding For Long Polar Codes
authors: Zhongjun Yang, Zhichen Liu, Li Chen, Xianbin Wang, Huazi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Soft information perturbations can significantly improve the successive cancellation (SC) decoding performance of polar codes. This is an effective method for realizing low-latency yet high performance for long polar codes, since each perturbation-based SC (PSC) decoding can be performed in parallel. However, little theoretical insight has been revealed so far regarding its work rationale. This paper provides the theoretical analysis of the soft information perturbation. It reveals that PSC decoding improves the SC decoding performance through correcting the erroneous bit estimations, especially the first erroneous bit (FEB). It further validates that perturbing the soft information does not degrade the error-correction capability of SC decoding. Such revelations lead to the design of optimal perturbations that maximizes the FEB correction probability, resulting in an enhanced PSC decoding performance. Based on this, a novel hybrid PSC (HPSC) decoding is proposed. By introducing the random and biased perturbations, the HPSC decoding can better divert from the initial erroneous estimation and converge to the intended one. Our simulation results demonstrate that with the optimal perturbation, the HPSC decoding can achieve a similar performance as the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) aided SC list (CA-SCL) decoding, while avoiding path sorting and expansion.
tldr: The paper provides a theoretical analysis of soft-information perturbation in successive-cancellation decoding of polar codes and proposes a hybrid perturbation-based SC (HPSC) decoder for long polar codes.
motivation: Perturbation-based SC decoding improves polar code performance and enables parallel low-latency decoding, but its working rationale had little theoretical grounding and no principled way to choose perturbations.
method: The authors analyze PSC decoding theoretically, showing it works by correcting erroneous bit estimates—especially the first erroneous bit (FEB)—and design optimal random and biased perturbations, combining them into a hybrid PSC (HPSC) decoder.
result: Simulations show that with optimal perturbations, HPSC achieves performance comparable to CRC-aided SC-list decoding over long polar codes while avoiding path sorting and expansion.
conclusion: Perturbation of soft information does not degrade SC error-correction capability, and optimized perturbation design yields near-CA-SCL performance at lower complexity.

title: When Pebbles Are Not Atomic: A Polynomial Separation Between Pure And Entangled Pebbling
authors: Piotr Marszalik
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph pebbling is the model in which the memory cost of memory-hard functions and proofs of space is measured, and pebbling lower bounds are the main way to argue that such constructions are secure. It has long seemed that the model is faithful to reality. It is known that it is not exact: an adversary who stores encoded information instead of whole values can do better, but so far only by small factors: a factor of 1.5 in the work that introduced entangled pebbling (Alwen, Chen, Kamath, Kolmogorov, Pietrzak and Tessaro) and, recently, a factor of about log n/log log n (de Rezende, Engstr\"om and Reyzin). One could still hope that pebbling is right up to such small factors. In pure pebbling, memory consists of whole labels; entangled pebbling also allows encoded state, such as XORs of labels. We show that the two models can differ polynomially. We study the setting in which proofs of space and data-dependent memory-hard functions are used: a state is prepared in advance, a random challenge has to be answered from it, and memory is paid for as long as it is held. Our graphs are explicit and have indegree two, and on them a pure adversary can do no better, up to a constant factor, than storing every possible answer in advance. Still, an adversary who keeps XORs instead of labels pays polynomially less. This ends the hope that pure pebbling is a faithful model of memory up to small factors. The heart of the paper is a simple combinatorial game, together with a special class of graphs found by Alon, Moitra and Sudakov.
tldr: The paper proves a polynomial separation between pure graph pebbling and entangled pebbling, showing that storing encoded (XOR) states can beat whole-label storage by a polynomial factor on explicit indegree-two graphs, undermining pure pebbling as a faithful memory model for proofs of space and memory-hard functions.
motivation: Pebbling lower bounds underpin security arguments for memory-hard functions and proofs of space, and prior work showed only small (constant or log n/log log n) gaps between pure and entangled pebbling, leaving hope that the pure model was faithful up to small factors.
method: The author constructs explicit indegree-two graphs, building on a graph family of Alon, Moitra and Sudakov, and analyzes a simple combinatorial game in the setting where a state is prepared in advance and a random challenge must be answered while memory is paid for as long as it is held.
result: On these graphs a pure adversary can do no better, up to a constant, than storing all possible answers in advance, yet an adversary keeping XORs of labels pays polynomially less memory, establishing a polynomial separation between the two models.
conclusion: Pure pebbling is not a faithful model of memory up to small factors, which has consequences for the security analysis of data-dependent memory-hard functions and proofs of space.

title: Phase-dependent THz Yield In Two-color Laser Plasmas: Nonlinear Propagation And Coulomb-modified Recollision
authors: Yange Chen, Ahai Chen, Jiahui Guo, Tianmin Yan, Yizhu Zhang, Yuhai Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-color laser-induced plasmas provide a reliable source of broadband terahertz (THz) radiation and offer several control parameters for optimizing THz yields. We investigate the phase-dependent THz yield (PTY) driven by a two-color laser field with parallel linear polarizations, using a model that couples macroscopic nonlinear propagation and microscopic Coulomb effects. Comparisons with models accounting for either effect alone show that their coupled effects shift the yield extrema and reshape the phase-dependent response. Nonlinear propagation distorts the local laser waveform, while the Coulomb interaction modifies the subsequent electron dynamics, particularly recollision. These changes modify the directional asymmetry of the photoelectron momentum distribution and hence the THz emission. Within the studied range, the combined model predicts a larger shift of the optimal phase than either effect alone, together with a reduced phase separation between the yield maximum and its adjacent minimum. These findings may guide THz optimization with more complex driving fields.
tldr: The paper models phase-dependent terahertz emission from two-color laser-induced plasmas by coupling nonlinear laser propagation with Coulomb-modified electron recollision dynamics.
motivation: Two-color laser plasmas are a practical broadband THz source, and optimizing the THz yield requires understanding how macroscopic propagation and microscopic Coulomb effects jointly shape the phase dependence.
method: The authors compare a coupled model of nonlinear propagation and Coulomb-modified recollision against models including only one of these effects, analyzing shifts in the optimal phase and photoelectron momentum asymmetry.
result: The coupled effects shift the THz yield extrema and reshape the phase-dependent response more strongly than either effect alone, while reducing the phase separation between the maximum and adjacent minimum.
conclusion: Accounting for both nonlinear propagation and Coulomb effects is important for predicting optimal two-color THz generation and may guide optimization with more complex driving fields.

title: Gerchberg-Saxton Optimized Silicon Metasurface For Sinusoidal Structured-Light Three-Dimensional Imaging
authors: Shuming Wang Gengyuan Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging based on structured illumination has attracted considerable attention in applications including machine vision, robotics, and computational sensing. However, conventional structured-light systems generally rely on bulky projection components, such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which limit system miniaturization and integration. Here, we demonstrate a compact structured-light 3D imaging platform enabled by a silicon dielectric metasurface operating at a near-infrared wavelength of 940 nm. The desired sinusoidal fringe illumination is encoded into the metasurface through a Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) phase optimization algorithm, which converts the target far-field distribution into a nanoscale phase profile and subsequently into silicon nanopillar geometries. The fabricated metasurface generates high-quality sinusoidal structured illumination, which is integrated with a four-step phase-shifting reconstruction method to recover 3D object profiles. The proposed approach provides a compact and scalable solution for miniaturized structured-light projection and optical 3D sensing.
tldr: A silicon dielectric metasurface designed via Gerchberg-Saxton phase optimization generates sinusoidal structured illumination at 940 nm for compact three-dimensional optical imaging.
motivation: Conventional structured-light 3D imaging systems rely on bulky projection optics such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which hinder miniaturization and system integration.
method: The target sinusoidal fringe field is converted into a nanoscale phase profile using a Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm and then mapped onto silicon nanopillar geometries; the fabricated metasurface is combined with a four-step phase-shifting reconstruction scheme to recover object profiles.
result: The fabricated metasurface produces high-quality sinusoidal structured illumination and, together with phase-shifting reconstruction, successfully recovers 3D object profiles in a compact platform.
conclusion: The approach offers a compact and scalable route to miniaturized structured-light projection and optical 3D sensing.

title: Shaping The Spectra Of Second Harmonic Laser By Spatial Focusing
authors: Yan-Ming Liu, Tao Xie, Xiangying Hao, Rui-Bo Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurately controlling the spectral width of second harmonic generation (SHG) is critical in applications such as nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, where tailored spectral properties are required. Although it is known that the focal length of the lens used to focus the pump beam influences the SHG spectrum, a simple and precise theoretical understanding of this effect has been lacking. Here, we develop a theoretical model to describe how pump focusing conditions affect SHG spectral broadening, and experimentally validate the model using BBO crystals with lenses of 50 mm and 200 mm focal lengths. Our results establish a practical method for engineering the SHG spectral width through pump focusing, providing valuable guidance for designing nonlinear optical systems with specific spectral requirements.
tldr: The paper develops and experimentally validates a theoretical model for controlling the spectral width of second harmonic generation through pump-beam focusing conditions.
motivation: Second harmonic generation spectral width is important for nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, but a simple precise theory of how focusing affects the SHG spectrum was lacking.
method: The authors derive a theoretical model for SHG spectral broadening under different pump focusing conditions and test it experimentally in BBO crystals using 50 mm and 200 mm focal-length lenses.
result: The model successfully describes how the lens focal length and spatial focusing influence the SHG spectral width, and the experimental measurements validate the predicted behavior.
conclusion: Pump focusing provides a practical method for engineering SHG spectral width, offering guidance for designing nonlinear optical systems with tailored spectral properties.

title: Counterexamples To The Total-current Hohenberg-Kohn Conjecture
authors: Mih\'aly A. Csirik Andre Laestadius
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian [MATH] has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian [MATH], with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge [MATH]. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.
tldr: The paper presents three counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture in three-dimensional spinless fermion systems.
motivation: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture is a foundational uniqueness claim in current-density-functional theory, and its validity is important for the theoretical basis of magnetic-field density functional approaches.
method: The authors construct explicit counterexamples using two spinless fermions in three dimensions, including noninteracting cases and an interacting Coulomb case with harmonic confinement and Dirac monopole fields, analyzing density and current degeneracies under complex conjugation.
result: Each counterexample gives two Hamiltonians with different magnetic fields but the same scalar potential, interaction, ground-state density, and zero total current, thereby violating the conjectured one-to-one mapping.
conclusion: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture fails in physically relevant three-dimensional settings, with implications for the foundations of current-density-functional theory.

title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
authors: Anna Kulter, Lorenz Wei{\ss}, David J. Grafinger, Alexander Sagar Grossek, Rodolfo Previdi, Martin Schultze, Marcus Ossiander
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. With a 0.9{\deg}-sensitivity for polarization rotations in a 1-second measurement and single-shot capability, the device opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast magneto-optic spectroscopy and at accelerator-based light sources.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a transmissive nanophotonic polarimeter for extreme ultraviolet (41 nm) light based on multimode channel-waveguide interference.
motivation: Polarization control in the extreme ultraviolet is hampered by the lack of transmissive optical elements, limiting ultrafast magneto-optic spectroscopy and lithography applications.
method: Channel waveguides restrict 41-nm light to a few modes with well-defined spatial profiles and propagation constants; designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes yields polarization-dependent forward scattering.
result: The device resolves the polarization axis and spectrum from a single measurement, achieving 0.9-degree sensitivity to polarization rotation in a one-second measurement with single-shot capability.
conclusion: The polarimeter opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast magneto-optic spectroscopy and at accelerator-based light sources.

title: Single Commutators In Schatten Ideals
authors: Shanshan Yang Zhichao Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that every operator in the Schatten [MATH]-class ([MATH]) can be realized as a single commutator of operators in the Schatten [MATH]-class. This settles the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.
tldr: The paper proves that every operator in a Schatten p-class can be expressed as a single commutator of two operators in the same Schatten class, resolving the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals.
motivation: The Pearcy-Topping question concerns whether elements of operator ideals can be represented as single commutators within the same ideal, a purely operator-theoretic structural problem.
method: The authors use functional-analytic and operator-ideal techniques to construct factors realizing any given Schatten-class operator as a single commutator, while also deriving simultaneous operator-norm and Schatten-norm bounds.
result: Every operator in the Schatten p-class is shown to be a single commutator of two operators in the same Schatten p-class, with explicit norm control on the factors.
conclusion: This settles the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals and provides quantitative commutator factorizations, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bibo Stability In Infinite Dimensions: Extensions And Limitations Of Finite-dimensional Theory
authors: Alexander A. Wierzba Sahiba Arora
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of infinite-dimensional systems gives rise to difficulties that do not occur in the classical finite-dimensional setting. In this paper, we resolve several questions concerning the definition and characterisation of BIBO stability in the framework of system nodes. In particular, we show that [MATH]-BIBO stability need not imply [MATH]-BIBO stability in general, but that the two notions are equivalent when the output space is reflexive. Furthermore, we investigate to what extent classical results extend to the infinite-dimensional setting, including the relation between BIBO stability and exponential stability under controllability and observability assumptions.
tldr: A functional-analytic study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability for infinite-dimensional linear systems described by system nodes, clarifying how the finite-dimensional theory extends and where it fails.
motivation: BIBO stability in infinite dimensions behaves pathologically compared to the classical finite-dimensional setting, and several basic questions about its definition and characterization within the system-node framework remained unresolved.
method: Abstract operator-theoretic analysis of system nodes, comparing L^p-type BIBO notions, proving implications and counterexamples, and invoking reflexivity of the output space to recover equivalences.
result: L^1-BIBO stability does not in general imply L^2-BIBO stability, but the two coincide when the output space is reflexive; classical links between BIBO stability and exponential stability are shown to survive under controllability and observability assumptions.
conclusion: The paper delimits precisely which parts of finite-dimensional stability theory carry over to infinite dimensions, providing corrected definitions and characterizations for system nodes.

title: Global Exact Controllability For Schr\"odinger Equations With Lipschitz And Logarithmic Nonlinearities
authors: Xiuting Li Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study global exact controllability of semilinear Schr\"odinger equations by localized internal additive controls. For every globally Lipschitz nonlinearity in arbitrary dimensions, we prove that any two [MATH] states can be connected in any prescribed positive time, without smallness assumptions on the states or the Lipschitz constant. The result holds on smooth bounded Euclidean domains under a local convex-phase condition, and on an interval with any nonempty open control region. It also extends to compact Riemannian manifolds under the corresponding phase condition. In one dimension, we further establish controllability for logarithmic nonlinearities of the form \[ f(z)=z\phi(|z|)+\mathfrak g(z), \] where [MATH] is real-valued, [MATH] is globally Lipschitz, and [MATH] with [MATH]. For the endpoint case [MATH], we achieve the result by assuming the leading coefficient is sufficiently small. These results resolve the global Lipschitz controllability question raised by Zuazua \cite[Section~3]{Zuazua2003} in the stated geometric settings and establish its logarithmic extension within the specified one-dimensional classes.
tldr: The paper proves global exact controllability results for semilinear Schrödinger equations with locally Lipschitz and logarithmic nonlinearities using localized internal controls.
motivation: Global controllability for semilinear Schrödinger equations with arbitrary Lipschitz constants and no smallness assumptions was an open question raised by Zuazua; the authors aim to resolve it and extend it to logarithmic nonlinearities.
method: The authors use localized internal additive controls and, in one dimension, handle the endpoint case by assuming a sufficiently small leading coefficient; the analysis rests on a local convex-phase geometric condition on smooth bounded domains, intervals, and compact Riemannian manifolds.
result: They show that any two H^1 (or similar) states can be connected in any prescribed positive time for every globally Lipschitz nonlinearity in arbitrary dimensions, and they establish one-dimensional controllability for logarithmic nonlinearities of the form f(z)=z phi(|z|)+g(z).
conclusion: The work settles the global Lipschitz controllability question in the stated geometric settings and provides a logarithmic extension within specified one-dimensional classes.

title: BR-MoE: Budgeted Semantic Release For Privacy-Preserving Traffic Analytics
authors: Abdolazim Rezaei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic cameras support useful analysis, but their outputs can reveal private information. Replacing images with text reduces direct visual exposure. It does not place a formal bound on disclosure. The published reinforcement learning and mixture-of-experts framework refines scene descriptions through relevance, coverage, and brevity rewards. It does not account for repeated releases under a fixed privacy budget. This paper proposes budgeted semantic release as an extension of that framework. Four scene experts first process isolated video chunks. Their outputs are mapped to a fixed, bounded semantic schema. A reinforcement learning controller selects which expert summaries to release and how much privacy budget to spend. The controller uses public task requests and previous private releases. A separate privacy filter enforces the total budget. Calibrated noise is added before the summaries are converted to text. Under explicit chunk isolation and bounded-event assumptions, the complete release transcript satisfies an event-level differential privacy bound. The design also supports reuse of previous summaries without new disclosure. An evaluation protocol covers traffic utility, privacy attacks, release freshness, and computational cost. Illustrative tables show the intended reporting format. They do not establish empirical gains. The proposed contribution is a task-aware release interface with auditable privacy accounting for repeated traffic descriptions.
tldr: The paper proposes a budgeted semantic release framework that combines scene-expert mixture-of-experts summaries, reinforcement-learning release control, and calibrated noise to give event-level differential privacy guarantees for repeated traffic-camera descriptions.
motivation: Traffic cameras enable useful analytics but their outputs leak private information; replacing images with text reduces visual exposure without providing a formal disclosure bound, and existing RL/MoE scene-description frameworks ignore repeated releases under a fixed privacy budget.
method: Four scene experts process isolated video chunks and map outputs to a bounded semantic schema; an RL controller selects which summaries to release and how much privacy budget to spend, with a separate privacy filter adding calibrated noise before text conversion.
result: Under explicit chunk-isolation and bounded-event assumptions, the complete release transcript satisfies an event-level differential privacy bound, and prior summaries can be reused without additional disclosure; only an evaluation protocol and illustrative reporting tables are given, with no empirical gains established.
conclusion: The contribution is a task-aware release interface with auditable privacy accounting for repeated traffic descriptions, but it remains a design proposal without experimental validation and lies outside quantum information science.

title: On The Support Geometry And Complexity Of Labs
authors: William Cruz-Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LABS are a fundamental combinatorial optimization problem arising in sequence design and statistical physics, yet the formal complexity of the standard fixed-geometry problem remains unresolved. We study how zero-energy complexity changes when support geometry is included as part of the input and then progressively restricted. For unary standard LABS, we establish membership in [MATH] and a sparsity/Mahaney consequence: Karp NP-hardness would imply [MATH]. For Pair-Set-LABS and Masked-LABS, zero-energy feasibility is polynomial-time decidable when every pair group or masked row has at most three terms and is NP-complete when four terms are allowed. NP-completeness persists when active supports are restricted to contiguous intervals.
tldr: The paper analyzes the computational complexity of the LABS combinatorial optimization problem when support geometry is included in the input and progressively restricted.
motivation: LABS arises in sequence design and statistical physics, but the formal complexity of the standard fixed-geometry problem remains unresolved, motivating a study of how adding support geometry to the input changes zero-energy complexity.
method: The authors establish complexity-theoretic membership and hardness results for unary standard LABS, Pair-Set-LABS and Masked-LABS, including sparsity/Mahaney-style consequences and restrictions to contiguous interval supports.
result: Unary standard LABS is shown to lie in a stated complexity class with the consequence that Karp NP-hardness would imply a collapse; for Pair-Set-LABS and Masked-LABS, zero-energy feasibility is polynomial when groups have at most three terms but NP-complete at four, even for contiguous interval supports.
conclusion: Support geometry strongly affects the complexity of LABS feasibility, giving sharp three-versus-four term thresholds and persisting hardness under interval-structured supports.

title: Big Secrets Small Shares: Revisiting Secure Multi-Party Computation
authors: Wilton Kim, van Long Phuoc Pham, Stanislav Kruglik, Han Mao Kiah
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At CRYPTO 2007, Damg{\aa}rd and Nielsen introduced a preprocessing approach to multi-party computation (MPC) to achieve linear communication complexity. Another approach to reduce communication complexity was proposed by Cramer, Damg{\aa}rd, and de Haan at EUROCRYPT 2007, which involved using ramp-secret sharing schemes to jointly share base-field components of secrets from the extension field. In this paper, we combine these two ideas to achieve a non-asymptotic reduction of communication cost in a multi-phase MPC setup. We introduce a new modification of the ramp secret sharing scheme, called compact sharing, and tailor the MPC protocol to accommodate this modification. Compact sharing masks the polynomial coefficients that would otherwise leak during degree reduction. The protocol provides perfect security against static semi-honest adversaries under an explicit tradeoff between the corruption threshold and the extension degree. When the extension degree scales linearly with the number of parties, the gate-evaluation core achieves constant communication overhead relative to an extension-field element, amortized over full preprocessing batches; input and output communication is counted separately.
tldr: The paper combines preprocessing and ramp secret sharing to reduce communication in secure multi-party computation via a new compact sharing scheme.
motivation: MPC protocols with many parties suffer from high communication cost, motivating techniques that amortize or reduce communication during gate evaluation and preprocessing.
method: The authors modify ramp secret sharing into compact sharing, which masks polynomial coefficients leaked during degree reduction, and tailor a multi-phase MPC protocol around it.
result: The protocol achieves perfect security against static semi-honest adversaries with an explicit corruption-threshold versus extension-degree tradeoff, and constant amortized gate-evaluation communication overhead when extension degree scales linearly with parties.
conclusion: Compact sharing enables non-asymptotic communication savings in MPC, though the work is classical cryptography and not aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: A Unified Attack Framework Against Statistical Generative Watermarks For Large Language Models
authors: Romina Omidi, Nima Naderloui, Yuan Hong, Binghui Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Watermarking has emerged as a key tool for identifying text generated by large language models (LLMs), with current schemes embedding statistical signals into the generation process to enable later detection. In this work, we identify a shared weakness across a broad class of popular LLM watermarking methods, including KGW (and its variants), GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS, and SynthID. We show that these schemes exhibit a fundamental link between their detection scores and the token probability shifts they introduce during generation. This link, which we call score-ratio alignment, allows an attacker with only black-box query access to the model--and no knowledge of secret keys or model weights--to produce text that evades detection while remaining fluent and natural. We prove that the resulting attack is optimal across all covered watermark families, and show that the weakness is intrinsic: any watermark designed to maximize statistical detection power necessarily induces the very structure that attackers can exploit. We evaluate our attack on seven popular generative LLM watermarking schemes, three LLMs, and tasks, which reduce detection rates to at most 0.05 across all settings while preserving text quality. Our findings show that current watermarking methods can be reliably defeated under realistic attack conditions, highlighting the need for fundamentally different watermarking designs that decouple detection scores from token probability shifts.
tldr: The paper identifies a shared structural weakness ('score-ratio alignment') in a broad class of statistical LLM watermarking schemes and exploits it with a black-box evasion attack that is proven optimal for the covered watermark families.
motivation: LLM watermarking is used to detect machine-generated text, but it is unclear whether the statistical signals embedded during generation are robust against adversaries who only have query access to the model.
method: The authors show that detection scores of KGW/GumbelSoft/DipMark/ITS/SynthID style watermarks are tightly linked to the token-probability shifts they induce, and design a black-box attack that exploits this link to generate fluent text with suppressed detection scores, proving optimality within the covered families.
result: Across seven watermarking schemes, three LLMs, and multiple tasks, the attack reduces detection rates to at most 0.05 while preserving text quality, and the weakness is shown to be intrinsic to any watermark maximizing statistical detection power.
conclusion: Current statistical generative watermarks can be reliably defeated under realistic black-box conditions, motivating new designs that decouple detection scores from token-probability shifts.

title: A Noise-level-free Parameter-choice Rule For Iterated Lavrentiev Regularization Of Nonlinear Potential Monotone Ill-posed Problems
authors: Hemant Sharma Ankit Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations [MATH] in a Hilbert space, where [MATH] is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fr\'echet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution [MATH] (a locally operator), and only noisy data [MATH] with unknown noise norm [MATH] is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^\delta=x_k^\delta-\bigl(F'(x_k^\delta)+\alpha_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta+\alpha_k(x_k^\delta-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require [MATH]. We analyze a parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer [MATH] of [MATH] over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and [MATH]. If moreover [MATH] and [MATH], we prove [MATH] with the computable [MATH] satisfying [MATH], yielding the baseline rate [MATH] along admissible growing-horizon families, and [MATH] whenever [MATH]; no range-invariance or tangential cone conditions are imposed. Rates under H\"older source conditions with [MATH] (including saturation) follow; the case [MATH], the removal of the self-adjointness assumption, and a full oracle inequality are identified as open problems.
tldr: The paper proposes a retrospective parameter-choice rule for nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear monotone ill-posed operator equations when the noise norm is unknown.
motivation: Classical stopping rules for iterated Lavrentiev regularization require knowledge of the noise norm, which is often unavailable in practice.
method: The authors analyze a retrospective-type rule that selects a minimizer over a finite computed window and prove convergence and convergence rates under a standard noise condition and Hölder source conditions.
result: They obtain the baseline rate along admissible growing-horizon families, improved rates when an additional condition holds, and saturation results, without imposing range-invariance or tangential cone conditions.
conclusion: The proposed rule provides noise-level-free parameter selection for this class of nonlinear ill-posed problems, while several extensions such as the case of exponent one, removing self-adjointness, and a full oracle inequality remain open.

title: Convolution Quadrature With Adaptive History Compression For Variable-Order Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equations
authors: Paul Zegeling Pu Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a fully implicit fast method for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction--diffusion equations with periodic fractional diffusion and exponential-transition Scarpi memory. A Volterra-resolvent analysis establishes local well-posedness and temporal regularity estimates that describe the weak initial singularity. Backward Euler convolution quadrature combined with Fourier pseudospectral discretization achieves mesh-uniform stability and positive-time first-order convergence. To accelerate the scheme, we utilize Cauchy--FFT weight recovery and adaptive blockwise sum-of-exponentials compression, which significantly reduces the cost of history evaluation under local error control. A logarithmic perturbation bound quantifies the effects of weight recovery, history compression, and inexact nonlinear solves, giving tolerance conditions that preserve the convergence order. Numerical experiments confirm the first-order accuracy and demonstrate that the accelerated method efficiently resolves long-time spatial patterns at a substantially reduced computational cost.
tldr: A fully implicit fast numerical scheme for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction-diffusion equations using backward Euler convolution quadrature, Fourier pseudospectral discretization, and adaptive history compression.
motivation: Variable-order fractional reaction-diffusion models with Scarpi memory are computationally expensive because history evaluation of the convolution kernel scales poorly in long-time simulations, so a fast, stable, and accurate scheme is needed.
