We then demonstrate the utility of the dataset through exploratory analyses of doctoral production, institutional pathways, undergraduate preparation, mentorship networks, and research areas. This revealed patterns including large concentrations of doctoral production among a small number of institutions and advisors. Additionally, our analysis highlights the vital role of Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) in preparing Black women who have earned doctoral degrees in the mathematical sciences. By transforming historical documentation into structured research infrastructure, this work provides a foundation for future investigations of mathematical communities using historical as well as mathematical, statistical, and computational methods. More broadly, the framework developed here offers a model for constructing datasets that support the study of underrepresented communities within the mathematical sciences.
tldr: The paper builds a curated, verifiable dataset of 147 Black women who earned doctorates in the mathematical sciences in the United States and uses it for exploratory historical and statistical analyses.
motivation: Official records and historical accounts have fragmented or omitted the contributions of Black women in mathematics, and this documentary absence is itself a mechanism of exclusion that the authors aim to remedy.
method: The authors combine archival research, institutional records, digital databases, and community knowledge to define a reproducible protocol for identifying and verifying individuals, then perform exploratory analyses of doctoral production, institutional pathways, undergraduate preparation, mentorship networks, and research areas.
result: The analyses reveal strong concentration of doctoral production among a small set of institutions and advisors, and highlight the outsized role of Historically Black Colleges and Universities in preparing Black women who later earn mathematical sciences doctorates.
conclusion: By converting historical documentation into structured research infrastructure, the work provides a foundation and a transferable methodological model for studying underrepresented communities in the mathematical sciences.

title: On The Accuracy Of Approximate Leave-One-Out With Blockwise Nonsmooth Regularization In High-dimensions
authors: Honghao Lin, Songbin Liu, Arian Maleki, Vahab Mirrokni, Chen Shang, David P. Woodruff, Hanbo Yang, Wenjin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximate leave-one-out (ALO) refers to methods that provide computationally efficient and statistically accurate approximations to leave-one-out risk estimation. These methods have recently attracted increased attention because of their connections to other important problems, including machine unlearning and data valuation. For empirical risk minimization, ALO methods often rely on a few Newton steps and therefore require smooth loss functions and regularizers. In high-dimensional problems, however, regularizers are frequently non-smooth. This has motivated the development of heuristic ALO methods for non-smooth regularization, whose empirical accuracy is often strong but whose theoretical justification remains limited. In this paper, we study the accuracy of a heuristic ALO method for a broad class of non-differentiable penalties that promote block sparsity in the proportional high-dimensional regime. Assuming uniformly bounded block sizes, we prove that the expected average absolute discrepancy between the exact leave-one-out loss and its ALO approximation is [MATH]. Our proof technique differs substantially from existing approaches and relies on obtaining sharp bounds on the number of active groups whose status changes between the full-data and leave-one-out estimators. In addition to yielding stronger guarantees under weaker assumptions than prior work, our analysis provides new insight into the stability of sparse estimators under perturbations of the training data.
tldr: The paper proves accuracy guarantees for a heuristic approximate leave-one-out (ALO) method under blockwise nonsmooth regularization in the proportional high-dimensional regime.
motivation: ALO methods for risk estimation typically require smooth losses and regularizers, but high-dimensional problems often involve nonsmooth penalties; existing heuristic extensions lack theoretical justification.
method: The authors analyze a heuristic ALO procedure for a broad class of penalties promoting block sparsity, assuming uniformly bounded block sizes, and bound the expected average absolute discrepancy between exact LOO loss and its ALO approximation by controlling the number of active groups whose status changes between full-data and LOO estimators.
result: They obtain sharper bounds under weaker assumptions than prior work, establishing that the ALO approximation is accurate in the proportional high-dimensional regime and yielding new insight into the stability of sparse estimators under training-data perturbation.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical backing for heuristic ALO with nonsmooth block-sparsity regularization, with implications for machine unlearning and data valuation.

title: Trace Inverse Estimates And Kernel-based Nitsche Galerkin Methods For Elliptic Interface Problems
authors: Leevan Ling, Shu Ma, Weifeng Qiu, Yizhong Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish trace inverse estimates for products of independently generated Sobolev-kernel trial spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche Galerkin methods for elliptic interface problems. The estimates control one-sided gradient traces by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form provides the flux control required by the Nitsche formulation without imposing value constraints on the trial spaces, including configurations with an interior inclusion. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain coercivity and well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and [MATH] error bounds of orders [MATH] and [MATH] for piecewise [MATH] solutions, [MATH], where [MATH] is the maximum fill distance and [MATH] is the kernel Sobolev order. The [MATH] bound additionally requires piecewise [MATH] regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For scaled kernels [MATH] with [MATH], we also derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and support scaling, whereas a three-dimensional mixed-boundary calculation illustrates the method.
tldr: The paper derives trace inverse estimates for products of Sobolev-kernel trial spaces and uses them to prove well-posedness and convergence of symmetric Nitsche Galerkin methods for elliptic interface problems.
motivation: Kernel-based meshfree methods for elliptic interface problems lack rigorous stability and error analysis, particularly trace control of one-sided gradients needed by Nitsche-type formulations without constraining trial-space values.
method: Trace inverse estimates are established for products of independently generated Sobolev-kernel spaces on Lipschitz subdomains, in a conormal form giving flux control; these are combined with a symmetric Nitsche Galerkin discretization and a scale-explicit condition-number analysis in the kernel-translate basis.
result: For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and fixed kernel scale, coercivity and well-posedness hold for sufficiently large penalty independent of refinement, with energy and L2 error bounds of orders related to the fill distance and kernel Sobolev order, verified in planar and 3D numerical experiments.
conclusion: The estimates provide a rigorous foundation for Nitsche-type kernel Galerkin methods on interface problems, assuming exact geometry and integration and requiring piecewise regularity of the adjoint interface problem for the L2 bound.

title: A Unified Theory Of Solvability For Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Control Problems I: The Homogeneous Case
authors: Hongwei Mei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existing theory of stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems focuses on open-loop and closed-loop solvability. For finite horizon problems, it is widely accepted that those two types of solvability are not equivalent in general, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples. In contrast, they coincide in standard infinite-horizon formulations with constant coefficients under suitable stabilizability and integrability assumptions. This paper aims at challenging this well-established paradigm by developing a novel framework of closed-loop solvability, namely generalized closed-loop solvability, which removes the [MATH]-integrability constraint on the feedback strategies from the existing formulation. It will be proven that open-loop and generalized closed-loop solvability are equivalent and the classical closed-loop solvablity is a particular case only when the admissible feedback strategy is [MATH]-integrable over the time horizon. In other words, the previously established non-equivalence between open-loop and closed-loop solvability stems solely from the limitations of the classical formulation which requires the [MATH]-integrability of the admissible feedback strategies over the time-horizon. Therefore, this paper unifies the theory of the solvabilitiy for stochastic LQ control problems. Moreover, our results offer a novel insight to stochastic LQ control problems: open-loop/generalized closed-loop solvability is essentially equivalent to piecewisely local closed-loop solvability in the classical sense. The current paper is focused on homogeneous cases only and non-homogeneous cases will be studied in a subsequent paper.
tldr: The paper introduces a 'generalized closed-loop solvability' framework for stochastic linear-quadratic control problems, proving equivalence between open-loop and (generalized) closed-loop solvability in homogeneous finite-horizon settings.
motivation: Standard stochastic LQ theory holds that open-loop and closed-loop solvability differ for finite horizons, due to counterexamples; the author argues this gap is an artifact of an overly restrictive square-integrability condition on feedback strategies.
method: A new solution concept is defined by dropping the L^2-integrability requirement on admissible feedback strategies, and the paper proves equivalence of open-loop and generalized closed-loop solvability, showing classical closed-loop solvability is a special case and is equivalent to piecewise-local closed-loop solvability.
result: Open-loop, generalized closed-loop, and piecewise-local classical closed-loop solvability are shown to be equivalent in the homogeneous case, unifying the previously separate notions and explaining the origin of earlier non-equivalence counterexamples.
conclusion: The work reframes the classical non-equivalence result as a formulation artifact and unifies the solvability theory for stochastic LQ control, with non-homogeneous cases deferred to a follow-up paper.

title: Ergodicity Of The Geodesic Flow On Surfaces Of Nonpositive Curvature
authors: Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Jana Rodriguez Hertz, Weisheng Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a full proof that the geodesic flow of a closed surface of genus at least two with a \(C^{3+}\) metric of nonpositive curvature is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. In a forthcoming paper, we will present the corresponding result for smooth rank-one manifolds in every dimension.
tldr: A rigorous proof that the geodesic flow on a closed genus-≥2 surface with a C^3+ nonpositively curved metric is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure.
motivation: Ergodicity of geodesic flows on negatively and nonpositively curved manifolds is a long-standing question in smooth ergodic theory, with the nonpositive-curvature surface case requiring methods beyond the classical Anosov/Hopf arguments.
method: The authors develop a complete dynamical-systems argument, presumably combining Pesin theory, invariant-manifold constructions for rank-one behavior, and careful control of flat and higher-genus structures, to establish ergodicity of the Liouville measure.
result: The main theorem gives a full proof of ergodicity for all C^3+ nonpositively curved metrics on closed surfaces of genus at least two, with an announced extension to smooth rank-one manifolds in arbitrary dimension.
conclusion: The work closes a classical problem in ergodic theory of geometric flows; it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Absolute Winning Properties Of Exceptional Sets For Rational Maps
authors: Haoyang Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Schmidt's game on the Julia set [MATH] of weak hyperbolic rational maps [MATH]. For each [MATH], let [MATH] be the set of points in [MATH] whose forward orbits stay a positive distance from [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] is absolute winning on [MATH] for each [MATH]. To do this, we first prove the absolute winning property for the exceptional set associated to the critical points by a potential game argument, and then use uniform expansion to obtain the result for each target point [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that exceptional sets of weak hyperbolic rational maps — points on the Julia set whose forward orbits avoid critical points and target points — are absolute winning in Schmidt's game.
motivation: Schmidt's game and winning properties provide a robust, intersection-stable notion of 'large' sets in Diophantine approximation and complex dynamics; the authors aim to establish such a strong largeness property for dynamically defined exceptional sets.
method: The authors first prove absolute winning for the exceptional set associated with the critical points via a potential-game (punctured neighbourhood) argument, then use uniform expansion of weak hyperbolic rational maps to transfer the property to each individual target point.
result: For every target point in the Julia set and every positive distance parameter, the corresponding exceptional set is shown to be absolute winning on the Julia set, implying in particular full Hausdorff dimension and stability under countable intersections.
conclusion: Absolute winning is thus established for dynamically defined exceptional sets of rational maps, extending Schmidt-game techniques beyond the classical linear/Diophantine setting.

title: The Dimension Landscape Of Bivariate $c^2$ Splines
authors: Jiansong Deng Xinyu Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schumaker's lower bound incorporates local geometric corrections and provides insight into the dimensions of bivariate spline spaces. Building on this bound, we study bivariate [MATH] spline dimensions from three perspectives: universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps. We prove universal attainment in degree seven for every legal realization of every triangulation. We prove generic attainment in degrees five and six for every fixed combinatorial triangulation and give explicit polynomial conditions certifying generic failure on fixed triangulations in degrees three and four. For geometric jumps with matching local direction types at corresponding interior vertices, we prove nonexistence in degree seven and construct examples in degrees three and five. In degree six, universal attainment and the existence of such geometric jumps remain open questions.
tldr: The paper analyzes dimensions of bivariate C^2 spline spaces on triangulations, extending Schumaker's lower bound via questions of universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps.
motivation: Schumaker's lower bound gives local geometric corrections for spline space dimensions, but it is unclear when this bound is actually attained and when geometric configurations force larger dimensions.
method: Pure mathematical analysis of spline spaces: proofs of universal attainment in degree seven, generic attainment in degrees five and six with explicit polynomial conditions certifying failure in degrees three and four, plus constructions and nonexistence proofs for geometric jumps.
result: Universal attainment is proven for degree seven on all triangulations, generic attainment for degrees five and six, explicit certificates of generic failure in degrees three and four, nonexistence of geometric jumps in degree seven, and examples in degrees three and five; degree six remains open.
conclusion: The work maps out the dimension landscape of bivariate C^2 splines across degrees, resolving several attainment and jump questions while leaving degree six open.

title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method With Physically Motivated Coarse Space For Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
authors: Likun Qiu, Jianguo Huang, Xuejun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. However, the method usually leads to ill-conditioned linear systems with a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), limiting its application. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.
tldr: The paper introduces FETI-SAW, a two-level domain decomposition method with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space for efficient finite element simulation of surface acoustic wave devices.
motivation: Finite element simulation of SAW devices suffers from ill-conditioned linear systems with huge numbers of degrees of freedom due to high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and unbounded domains.
method: Building on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) framework, the authors construct a Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a physically motivated Rayleigh-wave coarse space for the Lagrange multiplier system, yielding iteration counts stable in subdomain number, frequency, and mesh size.
result: Numerical experiments on interdigital transducers and SAW resonators demonstrate the efficiency of FETI-SAW, and MATLAB/C++ source codes are released.
conclusion: The physically grounded coarse space yields a scalable, robust solver for SAW device simulation, though the work is purely a classical numerical analysis contribution.

title: InterType: Breaking The Single-Function Barrier In Neural Binary Type Inference
authors: Shan Wang, Tianming Cui, Stephen Mccamant, Antonia Zhai, Pen-Chung Yew
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variable type recovery is a critical task in binary reverse engineering, enabling downstream applications such as vulnerability discovery, malware analysis, and security enforcement. While recent Transformer-based models have demonstrated strong performance in type inference by learning instruction-level semantics, they predominantly operate within single-function boundaries (i.e. intra-procedural analysis), ignoring the rich type constraints that propagate across function calls. Empirical studies have shown that nearly 44% of variables in real-world binaries propagate across function boundaries as arguments or return values, representing a significant source of type information that intra-procedural models cannot exploit. In this paper, we propose InterType, a method that embeds inter-procedural analysis into a pre-trained Transformer model for binary type recovery. Our approach builds on CodeArt, a state-of-the-art Transformer model for stripped binary analysis, and extends it by incorporating caller-callee data flow dependencies during fine-tuning. Specifically, we extract data flow dependence for each caller-callee pair from disassembled binaries and construct training instances that provide the model with cross-function context. By exposing the Transformer to inter-procedural variable propagation patterns, our model learns to resolve types that depend on cross-function data flow. We evaluate InterType on the coreutils benchmark compiled with optimization levels O0 through O3. On O1 binaries, InterType improves recall by 2.76 percentage points, from 89.00% for the intra-procedural CodeArt baseline to 91.76%, corresponding to a 25.1% reduction in recall error rate (1 - recall).
tldr: InterType extends a pre-trained Transformer (CodeArt) with inter-procedural data-flow context to improve variable type recovery in stripped binaries.
motivation: Nearly 44% of variables in real-world binaries propagate across function boundaries, so intra-procedural type inference models miss a large source of type constraints.
method: The authors extract caller-callee data-flow dependencies from disassembled binaries and build cross-function training instances used to fine-tune the CodeArt Transformer for inter-procedural type inference.
result: On coreutils at O1, InterType raises recall from 89.00% to 91.76% (+2.76 pp), a 25.1% reduction in recall error rate, with evaluations across O0-O3.
conclusion: Embedding inter-procedural analysis into pre-trained binary-analysis Transformers yields measurable gains in type recovery, though the work stays within software reverse engineering.

title: Scrambled Multiply-with-Carry Pseudorandom Number Generators
authors: Sebastiano Vigna
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiply-with-carry (MWC) generators are very fast pseudorandom number generators whose quality depends on the choice of a multiplier, and is usually assessed by applying the spectral test to an associated multiplicative congruential generator. We show that the special form of the modulus imposes structural limitations on the lattice structure of every MWC generator, which the generalized MWC generators of Goresky and Klapper mitigate; in our tests, xoring each output with its carry removes them. Since these limitations make the usual worst-case criterion useless, we rank candidates by a weighted geometric mean of their figures of merit, which does not depend on their normalization, and suggest multipliers for generators with 64 to 256 bits of state. Along the way, we correct some errors in the literature. In the end, we propose MWC192X, a 64-bit generator with 192 bits of state that passes all tests we are aware of, and emits an output in half a nanosecond.
tldr: A classical number-theory study of multiply-with-carry (MWC) pseudorandom generators, showing structural limitations in their lattice structure and proposing improved multipliers plus a new 64-bit generator, MWC192X.
motivation: MWC generators are extremely fast PRNGs whose quality depends on the multiplier, typically judged via the spectral test on an associated multiplicative congruential generator; the authors aim to understand and overcome the intrinsic lattice weaknesses of the MWC modulus form.
method: They analyze the lattice structure imposed by the special MWC modulus, compare against generalized MWC generators of Goresky–Klapper, test xoring outputs with carries, and rank candidate multipliers using a normalization-independent weighted geometric mean of figures of merit.
result: Xoring each output with its carry removes the observed structural limitations in their tests, the proposed ranking yields recommended multipliers for 64- to 256-bit state generators, several literature errors are corrected, and MWC192X (192-bit state, 64-bit output, ~0.5 ns per output) passes all tests they know of.
conclusion: The work delivers practical, high-quality classical PRNG designs and a corrected methodology for evaluating MWC multipliers, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Simple Strategy-Iteration With Dantzig's Rule Is Not Strongly Polynomial On Turn-Based Deterministic Games
authors: Sanyou Mei
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study turn-based deterministic zero-sum games with discounted and long-run average costs. For discounted costs, we establish exponential and superpolynomial iteration lower bounds for the simple strategy-iteration method with Dantzig's rule under unrestricted costs and unit weights, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this shows for the first time that the method is not strongly polynomial even when all action costs belong to [MATH]. For long-run average costs, we establish an exponential iteration lower bound for termination of a Dantzig counterpart with unrestricted costs and prove that it admits a strongly polynomial implementation with unit weights.
tldr: The paper proves iteration lower bounds showing that simple strategy iteration with Dantzig's rule is not strongly polynomial for turn-based deterministic zero-sum games with discounted and long-run average costs.
motivation: Strategy iteration is a classical algorithm for solving zero-sum games, and understanding whether Dantzig-style pivoting rules admit strongly polynomial complexity is a fundamental question in algorithmic game theory.
method: The authors construct adversarial instances and derive exponential and superpolynomial iteration lower bounds for simple strategy iteration with Dantzig's rule under unrestricted costs and unit weights.
result: They establish exponential lower bounds for discounted and long-run average cost settings, and show a strongly polynomial implementation for a Dantzig counterpart under unit weights in the average-cost case.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that simple strategy iteration with Dantzig's rule is not strongly polynomial even under restricted cost structures, while identifying a setting where a variant admits strongly polynomial behavior.

title: Beyond The Prompt: Recovering Hidden Concepts In Text-to-Image Models
authors: Minghong Fang Zhengfeng Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-image models can generate visual concepts that their prompts never mention, and recent work shows that such associations can be implanted so that ordinary prompts trigger them. Auditing this behavior requires recovering the description that a prompt omits. Existing prompt optimizers are not well suited to this task. Gradient-based methods require backward access to the scoring encoder. Discrete evolutionary search treats semantically unrelated tokens as equally close. Language-model-guided search requires one inference call per candidate, which limits exploration. This paper presents EmbGA, an embedding-space genetic algorithm that recovers concepts present in a set of images but absent from the prompt that generated them. EmbGA keeps the population structure of genetic search but applies its operators in the token embedding space. Crossover interpolates between parent embeddings, and mutation moves an embedding toward a randomly drawn vocabulary embedding. Each offspring is then projected back to discrete tokens before scoring, so every evaluated candidate is a valid token sequence. We evaluate EmbGA on two benchmarks against six optimizers under two exploration budgets. EmbGA achieves the highest alignment when the exploration budget is large, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.
tldr: EmbGA is an embedding-space genetic algorithm that recovers visual concepts present in generated images but missing from the original text-to-image prompt.
motivation: Text-to-image models can encode associations that ordinary prompts silently trigger, and auditing this requires recovering the omitted description, which existing prompt optimizers handle poorly due to gradient access requirements, poor token-space semantics, or costly per-candidate language-model calls.
method: The authors keep the population structure of genetic search but apply crossover (interpolation between parent embeddings) and mutation (movement toward a random vocabulary embedding) in token-embedding space, projecting each offspring back to discrete tokens before scoring so every candidate is a valid sequence.
result: On two benchmarks against six optimizers under two exploration budgets, EmbGA achieves the highest alignment at large budgets, recovers the most grounded tokens on natural images, and runs much faster than language-model-guided search.
conclusion: Embedding-space genetic search offers an efficient and effective way to audit hidden concept implantation in text-to-image models.

title: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose In Llm Agents
authors: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen, Carsten Maple
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents act through tools under per-action authorization: a local guard screens each tool call in isolation. We show that local authorization does not compose into global authorization. A compositional authorization failure (CAF) is a locally authorized execution, or a pair of locally authorized executions, that violates a global policy spanning intent, purpose, provenance, consent, and delegation. We characterize CAFs along two axes, expressiveness (single-trace safety versus relational k-safety) and observability (a ladder of monitor profiles). Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements. We make this constructive with AL-SYNTH, a SAT/SMT synthesizer (using no language model) that emits minimal CAF witnesses, each checked against an exhaustive oracle. The empirical signature is sharp: across nine LLM judges the per-action view approves the synthesized witness almost without exception, blocking it at a rate comparable to a benign control, yet the same models flag it when shown the two executions together. Per-action authorization is therefore structurally insufficient for relational policy conjuncts not reducible to single-trace safety: to bound them, a monitor must compare executions or accept false alarms.
tldr: The paper proves that per-action authorization for LLM agents cannot compose into global (relational) policy enforcement, since relational purpose violations are 2-safety hyperproperties with no per-trace locus of blame.
motivation: Autonomous LLM agents act through tools under local per-call guards, and practitioners implicitly assume that locally authorized actions yield globally authorized behavior, an assumption the authors show is structurally false.
method: The authors formalize compositional authorization failures along axes of expressiveness (single-trace safety vs. relational k-safety) and observability (monitor profiles), prove an impossibility result for per-action monitors, and build AL-SYNTH, a SAT/SMT-based synthesizer of minimal failure witnesses validated against an exhaustive oracle and tested on nine LLM judges.
result: Relational purpose violations are undetectable by any per-action monitor that avoids false alarms; empirically, all nine LLM judges approve the synthesized witnesses at rates comparable to benign controls yet flag them when shown the pair of executions jointly, and none of six surveyed guardrails implements cross-execution monitoring.
conclusion: Bounding relational policy conjuncts requires monitors that compare executions across traces or that accept false alarms; per-action authorization is structurally insufficient for LLM agent safety.

title: CyberHull: Deterministic Malicious Url Isolation Via Convex Hull
authors: Avijit Gayen, Aniket Ghosal, Durba Chakraborty, Sayan Mondal, Md Abdul Aziz Al Aman, Angshuman Jana
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of increasingly sophisticated and evasion-resistant phishing attack strategies represents a significant threat to modern cybersecurity, particularly in cyber-physical systems and internet-based networks. Traditional probabilistic methods and certain machine learning approaches often struggle to detect novel attacks and may lack interpretability or portability. To address these challenges, we introduce CyberHull, a resource-efficient and deterministic framework for identifying malicious URLs through mathematically defined convex hull boundaries across multiple orthogonal feature domains, including structural content entropy, hyperlink graph topology, and semantic token distribution. CyberHull constructs compact convex hulls, referred to as vaults, using the QuickHull algorithm, with a training complexity of O(n log n) under suitable assumptions. URL classification is performed through point-in-polyhedron tests that impose relatively low computational overhead on standard CPUs. Experimental results demonstrate that CyberHull achieves 92 percent detection accuracy, substantially outperforming a baseline linear approach based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which achieves 32 percent accuracy. Furthermore, CyberHull offers a computationally efficient alternative to resource-intensive deep learning approaches for malicious URL detection.
tldr: CyberHull is a deterministic malicious-URL detector that builds convex hull 'vaults' over hand-crafted feature domains and classifies URLs by point-in-polyhedron tests.
motivation: Probabilistic and deep-learning phishing detectors struggle with novel, evasion-resistant attacks and often lack interpretability and portability on constrained cyber-physical hardware.
method: URLs are mapped into multiple orthogonal feature spaces (structural content entropy, hyperlink graph topology, semantic token distribution); compact convex hulls are constructed with QuickHull at O(n log n) training cost, and classification uses point-in-polyhedron containment tests.
result: The framework reports 92% detection accuracy, versus 32% for a PCA-based linear baseline, while imposing low CPU overhead compared with deep learning alternatives.
conclusion: Geometry-based deterministic classification is presented as a lightweight, interpretable alternative to probabilistic and deep models for malicious URL detection.

title: Extending Mechanisms
authors: Noam Nisan Sergiu Hart
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an incentive-compatible mechanism for a single agent on a restricted domain of valuations, we consider its incentive-compatible extensions to the entire valuation space. We identify two extreme extensions: the "keep-the-menu" extension, which minimizes buyer payoffs and maximizes canonical prices pointwise, and the "keep-the-pricing" extension, which maximizes buyer payoffs and minimizes canonical prices pointwise.
tldr: The paper characterizes incentive-compatible extensions of a single-agent mechanism defined on a restricted valuation domain to the full valuation space, identifying two extreme extensions.
motivation: Mechanisms are often designed only for a restricted domain of valuations, so one needs a principled way to extend them to all possible valuations while preserving incentive compatibility.
method: A theoretical, game-theoretic analysis of single-agent incentive-compatible mechanisms, defining and comparing the 'keep-the-menu' and 'keep-the-pricing' extensions pointwise in terms of buyer payoffs and canonical prices.
result: The two extensions are shown to be extreme: 'keep-the-menu' minimizes buyer payoffs and maximizes canonical prices pointwise, while 'keep-the-pricing' does the opposite.
conclusion: The work provides a clean characterization of the boundary of incentive-compatible extensions, offering a framework for choosing among domain extensions in mechanism design.

title: Anchored Exploration In Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework For Semiconductor Designs
authors: Dawoon Jeong Huy Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.26973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.
tldr: A phylogenetic network framework is applied to 102,465 semiconductor products to distinguish cumulative design continuity from externally sourced feature additions.
motivation: The authors aim to model anchored exploration in technological evolution by separating continuity of design lineages from recombination via features borrowed from external precedents.
method: They build 45,996 design families from 102,465 semiconductor products and fit regressions quantifying horizontal transfer (HT) occurrence and descendant carriage of added features across the family support.
result: HT occurrence and descendant carriage show non-monotonic relationships, while within-family carriage increases over the observed support range.
conclusion: Product phylogenetics can disentangle the persistence of design lineage from the re-use of externally sourced features, informing how technological trajectories and recombination interact.

title: District Size Matters: How Seats Per District Shapes Proportionality Under Stv
authors: Daryl Deford, Thomas Ratliff, Ellen Veomett
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the impact of utilizing multimember districts and Single Transferable Vote (STV) as the winner selection method on partisan proportionality. We start with detailed case studies of the upper legislative houses of Illinois, New Hampshire, and New Mexico, building ensembles of redistricting maps with mostly 2-member, mostly 3-member, and mostly 4-member districts for each state. These ensembles are constructed using two methods: building from precincts, and merging currently existing single-member districts. We also compare two ballot generation models for each experiment: a modified Bradley-Terry model and a Plackett-Luce model. We find that our ensembles of multimember districts paired with STV have results which are centered closer to partisan proportionality than when single member districts are used. However, the choice of district size affects partisan outcomes enough that this choice could be exploited by a partisan mapmaker to advantage a particular party. The findings are consistent across all combinations of district construction and ballot generation models within a single state. We then expand our study to 41 different states, obtaining consistently similar proportionality results and allowing us to empirically evaluate the two ballot generation models, as implemented in VoteKit, at a national scale.
tldr: The paper studies how multimember district size under Single Transferable Vote affects partisan proportionality in U.S. state legislative redistricting.
motivation: The authors aim to understand whether multimember districts with STV improve proportional outcomes and whether district size choices can be exploited for partisan advantage.
method: They build ensembles of redistricting maps for Illinois, New Hampshire, and New Mexico using precinct-based construction and merging existing single-member districts, comparing Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce ballot models, then extend the analysis to 41 states.
result: Multimember districts with STV produce outcomes centered closer to partisan proportionality than single-member districts, but district size choices can shift partisan outcomes enough to be exploited by mapmakers.
conclusion: District size is a consequential design parameter for STV-based multimember systems, with implications for partisan fairness and empirical evaluation of ballot generation models at national scale.

title: Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes For A Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation With Nonlocal Pressure
authors: Hubert Woszczek {\l}ukasz P{\l}ociniczak
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study numerical approximations of the equation \partial_t^\alpha u-\nabla\cdot\left(u^{m-1}\nabla(-\Delta)^{-\sigma}u\right)=0, where [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH]. The Caputo derivative is discretized by the L1 formula, while the nonlinear nonlocal flux is approximated by a conservative upwind finite-difference scheme. We establish several structural properties of the implicit scheme in arbitrary space dimension, including a discrete maximum principle, non-negativity, mass conservation, [MATH] and [MATH] stability, existence of non-negative discrete solutions, and a discrete energy-dissipation estimate. Our assumptions include natural symmetry, a sign condition on the sum of the directional coefficients, and decay on the discrete weights. We also derive a consistency estimate for the complete nonlinear spatial operator. For rigorous convergence analysis, we restrict ourselves to one space dimension and introduce the cumulative variable associated with the density. This transforms the discrete problem into a monotone approximation of an equation involving the fractional Laplacian. Interestingly, for semigroup-based pressure-gradient weights, the resulting discrete operator is identified with the fractional discrete Laplacian. Next, using comparison and contraction properties of the integrated scheme, for [MATH] and under the stated spatial regularity and weighted temporal consistency assumptions, we prove uniform convergence of the cumulative numerical solution and convergence of the corresponding density against compactly supported smooth test functions. The temporal estimates allow a weak singularity at the initial time. We also analyze an explicit variant of the scheme and derive a sufficient CFL condition covering the full range [MATH].
tldr: The paper develops structure-preserving numerical schemes for a time-fractional porous medium equation with nonlocal pressure and proves convergence in one dimension.
motivation: The authors aim to provide robust numerical approximations for a nonlinear nonlocal fractional diffusion model while preserving key structural properties such as positivity, mass conservation, and energy dissipation.
method: They use the L1 scheme for the Caputo time derivative and a conservative upwind finite-difference discretization for the nonlinear nonlocal flux, then analyze an implicit scheme and an explicit variant via comparison and contraction arguments.
result: The implicit scheme satisfies a discrete maximum principle, non-negativity, mass conservation, stability, existence of non-negative solutions, and energy dissipation; uniform convergence of the cumulative solution and convergence of the density are proved in one space dimension under regularity assumptions.
conclusion: The work establishes rigorous structure-preserving numerical methods for a fractional porous medium equation with nonlocal pressure, though the topic lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks In Wireless Communications
authors: Gian Marti, Jakob Hoydis, Fay\c{c}al A\"it Aoudia, Sebastian Cammerer, Alexander Keller
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.
tldr: Sionna Bench proposes a benchmark framework for academic wireless communications research, piloted on MIMO-OFDM channel estimation.
motivation: Wireless communications lacks a benchmark tradition, causing methods for similar problems to be evaluated on incompatible setups and making comparison difficult.
method: The authors leverage AI-assisted coding to implement state-of-the-art methods at scale within a common framework, starting with twenty channel estimation methods from ten papers.
result: The pilot benchmark enables systematic comparison of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation methods against the state of the art.
conclusion: Benchmarks such as Sionna Bench could help navigate a research landscape increasingly populated by both AI-generated and human-developed algorithms.

title: Multiplicity Of Closed Geodesics On Odd-dimensional Bumpy Finsler Compact Space Form
authors: Linxinzi Qi Hui Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact space form, endowed with a bumpy Finsler metric [MATH]. In this paper, we prove that there exist at least [MATH] contractible minimal closed geodesics on [MATH], assuming that all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices. Here, a contractible closed geodesic is called minimal if it is not an iteration of any other contractible closed geodesic. In particular, this confirms the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture for the bumpy quotient manifold [MATH] under the non-zero Morse index assumption.
tldr: The paper proves a lower bound on the number of contractible minimal closed geodesics on compact odd-dimensional space forms equipped with bumpy Finsler metrics.
motivation: The work aims to extend multiplicity results for closed geodesics, in particular the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture, beyond the setting of Riemannian metrics to bumpy Finsler metrics on quotient manifolds.
method: Using Finsler geometry and Morse-theoretic techniques, the authors analyze the space of contractible closed geodesics and their Morse indices under a bumpiness assumption.
result: Assuming all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices, they show that at least a prescribed number of such geodesics exist, confirming the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture in this setting.
conclusion: The results establish new multiplicity lower bounds for closed geodesics in Finsler geometry and support the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture under the non-zero Morse index hypothesis.

title: Central Limit Theorems For Optimal Transport Functionals
authors: Haruki Kono
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish central limit theorems for empirical plug-in estimators of scalar functionals of quadratic optimal transport maps and potentials, including Wasserstein costs and several risk measures constructed from transport-based multivariate quantiles. We study the one-sample problem with a known reference distribution and i.i.d. observations from the target distribution. A natural approach is to combine a limit theorem for the empirical transport map with the functional delta method. We show, however, that in dimensions at least two, empirical transport-map errors admit no nonzero weak limit in [MATH] under any normalizing scale. Instead, we linearize the functional directly in the target distribution, obtaining an influence-function expansion with a remainder controlled by the transport-map error. The influence function is characterized by a linear elliptic partial differential equation. Under regularity conditions, we use this expansion to prove central limit theorems in low dimensions and establish validity of the empirical bootstrap. We also derive semiparametric efficiency bounds and show that the plug-in estimators attain them under the same conditions.
tldr: This paper proves central limit theorems for plug-in estimators of functionals of quadratic optimal transport maps and potentials.
motivation: Empirical optimal transport maps lack a nonzero weak limit in dimension at least two, so standard delta-method approaches fail for functionals such as Wasserstein costs and transport-based risk measures.
method: The author directly linearizes the target functional in the target distribution, derives an influence-function expansion controlled by transport-map error, and characterizes the influence function via a linear elliptic PDE.
result: Under regularity conditions, central limit theorems and bootstrap validity are established in low dimensions, and semiparametric efficiency bounds are shown to be attained by the plug-in estimators.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous statistical inference framework for optimal-transport-based functionals despite the instability of empirical transport maps in multivariate settings.

title: Model Exposure On One Device Endangers Others: Rethinking Edge Neural Network Security Across Devices
authors: Yuyang Zhang, Kangjie Chen, Yihui Jin, Run Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural networks (NNs) are increasingly deployed on edge devices such as mobile and IoT platforms, offering low latency and improved privacy compared to cloud-based deployment. However, on-device models embedded in mobile applications can be unpacked and exposed to adversaries, enabling cross-node attacks in centrally distributed ecosystems, where adversarial examples crafted on one compromised device transfer effectively to other nodes sharing the same models. To address this threat, we propose VeilNN, a defense framework that reduces adversarial transferability across on-device models via model obfuscation. The core idea of VeilNN is to introduce controlled model diversity while preserving original task functionality. Specifically, VeilNN applies stealthy and irreversible obfuscation at both the architectural and parameter levels through network cell obfuscation and layer assembling, and is applicable to diverse NN architectures, including MLPs, CNNs, and Vision Transformers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VeilNN effectively defends against cross-node attacks, achieving an average defense success of 49.19% and up to 81.19% across four adversarial attack types, with more than 33.16% improvement over existing defenses.
tldr: VeilNN is a model-obfuscation defense that injects controlled architectural and parameter-level diversity into on-device neural networks to stop adversarial examples crafted on one compromised edge device from transferring to others.
motivation: Models packed inside mobile/IoT apps can be extracted and attacked, and because many nodes in a distributed ecosystem run the same model, adversarial examples transfer across devices, so a single exposure endangers the whole deployment.
method: The framework applies stealthy, irreversible obfuscation at the network-cell and layer-assembly levels, preserving task accuracy while diversifying model instances, and is designed to work for MLPs, CNNs, and Vision Transformers.
result: Experiments across four adversarial attack types report an average defense success of 49.19% and up to 81.19%, exceeding existing defenses by more than 33.16%.
conclusion: Introducing deliberate model diversity is presented as an effective practical mitigation for cross-node adversarial transfer in edge AI ecosystems.

title: AgenticVulHunter: Bringing Local Agentic Vulnerability Hunting To Your Terminal
authors: Nishant Abhishek, Ping Charoenwet, Kla Tantithamthavorn
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding vulnerabilities early, before they can affect the production system, is important for reducing the risk of any software attacks. However, detecting vulnerabilities during secure code review is still difficult because the vulnerable code logic may depend on lines found across different repository files. Recent approaches such as AgenticSCR have shown that LLM agents can explore repository files and use security knowledge to improve secure code review. However, these approaches mainly rely on external commercial LLMs and can provide a large amount of security knowledge to the agent at once. This creates an important question of whether agentic secure code review can also be performed effectively using locally deployed open-weight LLMs with more focused and relevant security knowledge. In this paper, we propose AgenticVulHunter, an agentic secure code review approach and tool that can run with a locally deployed open-weight LLM. We evaluate AgenticVulHunter on 144 vulnerability cases from SCRBench using Qwen3-Coder-30B and DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus. We measure what percentage of generated review comments correctly identify the vulnerable location, match the vulnerability type, and provide a relevant security review comment together. AgenticVulHunter achieves an accuracy of 18.4% with Qwen3- Coder-30B and 23.8% with DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus, compared with 11.8% for our AgenticSCR-style reproduction using Qwen3-Coder-30B and 17.5% for AgenticSCR using Claude Sonnet 4.
tldr: AgenticVulHunter is a local LLM-agent tool for secure code review that detects vulnerabilities by exploring repository files with focused security knowledge.
motivation: Early vulnerability detection during code review is hard because vulnerable logic can span multiple repository files, and existing LLM-agent approaches rely on commercial external models.
method: The paper proposes an agentic secure code review approach and terminal tool using locally deployed open-weight LLMs, evaluated on 144 vulnerability cases from SCRBench with Qwen3-Coder-30B and DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus.
result: AgenticVulHunter achieves 18.4% accuracy with Qwen3-Coder-30B and 23.8% with DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus, outperforming an AgenticSCR-style reproduction at 11.8% and AgenticSCR with Claude Sonnet 4 at 17.5%.
conclusion: Local open-weight LLM agents can perform agentic secure code review effectively, though absolute accuracy remains modest and the work is outside quantum information research.

title: Knox: Hardware-assisted Regulatory Sandbox For Generative Models
authors: Vasisht Duddu, Adam Caulfield, Xi He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regulations require companies to run AI models in a regulatory sandbox, an isolated environment that enables monitoring model behavior by regulators, prior to deployment. But, they do not spell out the technical mechanisms to design such a sandbox. Ideally, a regulatory sandbox should show (i) compliance (checks against regulations, and deviations from intended behavior, i.e., unauthorized tool and system calls); (ii) confidentiality (protects model weights from regulators); (iii) attestability (produces tamper-resistant evidence of model behavior for monitoring); and (iv) scalability (evidence is verifiable by multiple regulators). Several prior works (information-flow control, prompt-injection defenses, control-flow integrity, and traditional sandboxing) address specific compliance aspects but lack confidentiality, attestability, and scalability. TEEs meet some of these requirements, but simply running models inside a TEE is insufficient as we need compliance mechanisms. We present KNOX, the first regulatory sandbox, built by running AI workloads inside TEEs. We demonstrate KNOX using agentic workloads. For compliance, we derive an attested policy manifest (with the applicable regulations, the expected tool calls, and the permitted system calls) for a given user prompt. Before an executor performs an action, an attested reference monitor compares it against the attested policy manifest and allows it only if it matches. Every action and verdict is recorded in an attested execution graph, enabling regulators to verify the model's execution and its compliance. We show that KNOX meets all requirements, and can check for compliance with regulations and deviations from intended behavior (e.g., due to prompt injection); and incurs low overhead (<1%).
tldr: KNOX is a hardware-assisted regulatory sandbox for generative AI models that uses trusted execution environments to enforce and attest compliance, confidentiality, and scalability.
motivation: Regulations increasingly require AI models to be deployed only after sandboxed monitoring, but existing technical mechanisms do not simultaneously provide compliance checks, model-weight confidentiality, tamper-resistant attestation, and multi-regulator scalability.
method: The authors run AI workloads inside TEEs and derive an attested policy manifest specifying applicable regulations, expected tool calls, and permitted system calls; an attested reference monitor checks each action against the manifest and records actions and verdicts in an attested execution graph.
result: KNOX is demonstrated on agentic workloads and is shown to satisfy the stated sandbox requirements, detect regulatory non-compliance and prompt-injection-induced deviations, and incur less than 1% overhead.
conclusion: KNOX provides a practical TEE-based architecture for regulatory sandboxing of generative models, though it is unrelated to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: HydraPoT: A Configurable Multi-Agent Framework For Cost-Aware LLM-Assisted Honeypots
authors: Kamolchanok Saengtong, Chutirat Saengyingyongwattana, Sasin Janpuangtong, Norrathep Rattanavipanon
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can improve honeypot realism by generating dynamic, context-aware responses, but powerful cloud models incur substantial cost and latency, while lightweight models may provide weaker deception. This forces practitioners to choose between operational efficiency and interaction fidelity. In this work, we present HydraPoT, a configurable multi-agent honeypot framework that integrates traditional emulation, lightweight LLMs, and powerful cloud LLMs. HydraPoT routes each attacker command to an appropriate agent according to a configurable complexity-based policy, while maintaining shared session state to preserve consistency across agent transitions. We evaluate HydraPoT through an architectural-overhead analysis, a cross-agent context-preservation benchmark, and a three-agent case study. HydraPoT introduces less than 5% runtime overhead, preserves context across heterogeneous agents, and achieves fidelity close to a cloud-LLM-only honeypot. Under our case-study policy, it reduces cloud-processed tokens by 72.6% and operational cost by 3.7x. These results demonstrate that configurable multi-agent routing can make realistic LLM-assisted honeypots more practical under limited operational budgets.
tldr: HydraPoT is a configurable multi-agent honeypot framework that routes attacker commands among traditional emulation, lightweight LLMs, and cloud LLMs to balance deception fidelity with operational cost.
motivation: LLM-assisted honeypots can improve realism, but powerful cloud models are costly and slow while lightweight models offer weaker deception, forcing a trade-off between fidelity and efficiency.
method: The framework routes each attacker command to an appropriate agent using a configurable complexity-based policy while maintaining shared session state across agent transitions, including traditional emulation and both lightweight and cloud LLMs.
result: HydraPoT introduces less than 5% runtime overhead, preserves context across heterogeneous agents, and achieves fidelity close to a cloud-LLM-only honeypot while reducing cloud-processed tokens by 72.6% and operational cost by 3.7x in the case study.
conclusion: Configurable multi-agent routing can make realistic LLM-assisted honeypots more practical under limited operational budgets.

title: Optimizing Flexibility And Commitments: Partially-Adaptive Multi-Stage Matrix Assembly Layout Design Problem
authors: Baturhan Bayraktar, Merve Bodur, Martin Grunow, Rainer Kolisch
abstract: ArXiv:2610.27401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matrix assembly layouts provide manufacturing flexibility under product variety and demand volatility through locally reconfigurable production stations. Periodic redesign exploits this flexibility, yet existing models allow only annual revisions. Finer calendars expose a flexibility-commitment trade-off: advance layout commitments support coordination, supplier agreements, and discounts. We introduce the layout revision timing problem, jointly choosing revision points and committed layout sequences under demand uncertainty while production adapts within those layouts. We formulate it as a partially adaptive multistage stochastic program with two complementary extensions. Our cost-based extension places the economic value of advance commitment in the objective rather than prescribing revision budgets; our scenario-adaptive extension adapts revision timing to revealed information. For station-use minimization, we establish a cost decomposition across commitment intervals, yielding an exact dynamic program that reuses station subproblem solutions across model variants and parameter settings. As a more general alternative, we develop an integer L-shaped method strengthened by monotonicity-based cuts for budgeted formulations and enhanced cuts exploiting this decomposition. On automotive instances, including scenario trees with nearly 10,000 nodes, our combined model's average savings in expected station-use cost at the base-case discount reach 4.99% versus full adaptivity and 28.65% versus full commitment. Scenario adaptivity is most valuable when demand paths diverge and discounts justify commitment on some paths but not others, as in electrification-driven scenarios.
tldr: The paper studies a partially adaptive multistage stochastic programming formulation for optimizing revision timing and committed layout sequences in matrix assembly layouts under demand uncertainty.
motivation: Manufacturing systems with high product variety and volatile demand can benefit from reconfigurable matrix assembly layouts, but existing models restrict redesign to annual revisions and ignore the trade-off between flexibility and advance commitment.
method: The authors introduce the layout revision timing problem, formulate it as a partially adaptive multistage stochastic program, and develop a cost-based extension, a scenario-adaptive extension, an exact dynamic program, and an integer L-shaped method with monotonicity-based and decomposition-enhanced cuts.
result: On automotive instances with scenario trees approaching 10,000 nodes, the combined model saves on average 4.99% in expected station-use cost versus full adaptivity and 28.65% versus full commitment at the base-case discount.
conclusion: The work provides optimization methods and managerial insight into when finer revision calendars and partial commitment are economically valuable, especially when demand paths diverge and discounts justify commitment selectively.
